subject.title: fix(sessions): large histories no longer load entire transcripts

question: Must schema v10 avoid a synchronous full-transcript rebuild on the first upgraded or dirty history request, or is that one-time request-path stall an accepted upgrade behavior?
rationale: The branch deliberately chooses lazy synchronous rebuilding, but that choice determines whether existing large sessions can still hit the reported availability problem immediately after upgrade or branch invalidation.

options.title: Move rebuild off requests
options.body: Prepare or chunk the projection outside history requests and switch bounded readers only after it is ready.

options.title: Accept one-time rebuilding
options.body: Explicitly accept the synchronous first-read cost after reviewing measured worst-case latency and memory proof from a large installed v9 database.

options.title: Pause the schema migration
options.body: Keep the existing reader until a projection strategy can guarantee acceptable upgrade and dirty-path behavior.

recommendation.title: Move rebuild off requests
recommendation.body: Prepare or chunk the projection outside history requests and switch bounded readers only after it is ready.

likelyOwner.reason: The recent session-storage architecture and this projection implementation are primarily connected to steipete's merged and proposed work.
